title: Wallaby — 5yo Bennett’s: facial swelling and drooling
presentation: 5-year-old male Bennett’s wallaby in a wildlife park, firm swelling along the left mandible for three weeks, drooling, dropping partly chewed food, and losing condition.

stages.title: Assess the animal and the enclosure
stages.briefing: BCS 2/5. Firm, warm, painful swelling over the left mandibular body with a draining tract at the gum margin. Ptyalism, quidding, foul oral odour. Left mandibular lymph node enlarged. Enclosure: fed on the ground on damp, trampled grass; concentrate pellets scattered on soil; several animals in the group, one with mild ptyalism.
stages.prompt: Which findings point to mandibular osteomyelitis?

options.label: Firm swelling of the mandibular body with a draining tract
options.detail: Bone infection reaching the surface

options.label: Quidding with a foul oral odour
options.detail: Necrotic oral tissue and impaired mastication

options.label: A second animal in the group with early ptyalism
options.detail: Shared risk in the same environment

options.label: Enlarged mandibular lymph node
options.detail: Expected drainage response to local infection

options.label: Ground feeding on damp trampled grass
options.detail: The husbandry driver, not a clinical finding

stages.explanation: Macropods develop necrobacillosis — "lumpy jaw" — when oral mucosa is abraded and Fusobacterium gets into bone, and the physical findings here are that disease. A second affected animal is the sign that this is an enclosure problem rather than one wallaby’s bad luck. The lymph node is a normal response, so it adds little to the localisation.

stages.title: Choose the tests
stages.briefing: The wallaby is anaesthetised, which is the only opportunity for a full oral and imaging assessment.

options.label: Skull radiographs or CT of the mandible
options.detail: Extent of lysis, sequestra, tooth involvement

options.label: Deep anaerobic and aerobic culture with sensitivity from the tract
options.detail: Fusobacterium is anaerobic and easily missed on routine culture

options.label: Cytology of the discharge
options.detail: Confirms suppuration and the organism type

options.label: Full oral examination with dental probing under anaesthesia
options.detail: Finds the entry point and any loose teeth

options.label: Haematology with total protein
options.detail: Systemic inflammatory burden and nutritional state

options.label: Mycobacterial culture as the primary investigation
options.detail: Granulomatous disease is worth excluding, but this is a classic necrobacillosis presentation

options.label: Faecal culture
options.detail: No relevance to mandibular osteomyelitis

stages.explanation: Anaerobic culture has to be requested specifically or Fusobacterium will not be found, and the sensitivity guides a long antibiotic course. Imaging decides whether this is treatable at all — extensive lysis with sequestra in a macropod carries a poor prognosis, and knowing that before you commit the animal to weeks of handling is kinder.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: CT: osteolysis of the left mandibular body with a 12 mm sequestrum, periosteal new bone, and involvement of two molar roots; no involvement of the temporomandibular joint. Culture: Fusobacterium necrophorum with Bacteroides species, sensitive to penicillin and metronidazole. Cytology: heavy suppuration with mixed bacteria. Oral examination: ulcerated gingiva around the affected molars with grass seed impaction. Haematology: neutrophilia, total protein 48 g/L with albumin 20 g/L. Mycobacterial culture negative.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Mandibular necrobacillosis with a bone sequestrum
options.detail: Fusobacterium with osteolysis and a sequestrum on CT

options.label: Grass seed impaction and gingival ulceration provided the entry point
options.detail: Ulcerated gingiva with impacted material at the affected teeth

options.label: Surgical debridement will be needed alongside antibiotics
options.detail: A sequestrum will not resolve on antibiotics alone

options.label: Ground feeding on contaminated soil is an enclosure-level risk
options.detail: A second animal affected, with the same feeding practice

options.label: Mycobacterial osteomyelitis is the diagnosis
options.detail: Culture negative

options.label: The temporomandibular joint is involved and the prognosis is hopeless
options.detail: CT shows the joint spared

stages.explanation: The sequestrum is the finding that determines the treatment plan: dead bone is a reservoir no antibiotic will reach, so this becomes a surgical case with medical support rather than a course of penicillin. A spared temporomandibular joint is genuinely good news and worth stating, because joint involvement is what usually decides euthanasia.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Fusobacterium necrophorum with Bacteroides from a mandibular tract, osteolysis with a 12 mm sequestrum and two involved molar roots, spared temporomandibular joint, gingival ulceration with grass seed impaction, albumin 20 g/L, one further affected animal.

options.label: Mandibular necrobacillosis (lumpy jaw) with sequestrum, on an enclosure-level husbandry risk
options.detail: Organism, lesion and the reason it happened

options.label: Mycobacterial osteomyelitis
options.detail: Culture negative

options.label: Dental root abscess without osteomyelitis
options.detail: Understates the lysis and the sequestrum

options.label: Oral squamous cell carcinoma
options.detail: Cytology and culture show suppuration and bacteria, not neoplasia

options.label: Traumatic mandibular fracture
options.detail: No fracture on CT; the lysis is infective

stages.explanation: The diagnosis commits to debridement of the sequestrum, extraction of the affected molars, a long penicillin or metronidazole course, and nutritional support for an animal with an albumin of 20 g/L. It also commits the park to raised feeders and drier feeding areas, because the second wallaby with ptyalism is the next case unless the enclosure changes.
